scope_note: Outcome labels apply to the named product, operator and domain scope. A failed or declining frontend does not silently classify a surviving token, blockchain, legal entity, licence or successor product.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers the bitcasino.io casino operated by Moon Technologies B.V. It excludes the separately linked Sportsbet.io sportsbook, payment-agent operations, and any inference that crypto deposits make the casino itself noncustodial or on-chain.

sources.notes: Current product, operator, licence claim, support and crypto-account surface.

sources.notes: Current operator-ledger, KYC, restrictions, withdrawals and product terms.

sources.notes: Official operator, company number, licence number and bitcasino.io domain certificate.

claims.evidence_locator: Terms identify Moon Technologies B.V. as owner and operator and define the account-based casino service.
claims.analyst_note: The linked Sportsbet.io product is excluded.

claims.evidence_locator: Current help center exposes registration, games, deposits, withdrawals, KYC, promotions and 24/7 support.
claims.analyst_note: Current service availability is not audited economic performance.

claims.evidence_locator: CGA certificate lists Moon Technologies B.V., company 152185, licence OGL/2023/111/0069 and bitcasino.io.
claims.analyst_note: Applies to the named entity, domain, activities and jurisdiction only.

licences.notes: CGA certificate reports the licence was extended under the LOK; this observation is not a licence for linked brands in other jurisdictions.

outcome.label: successful
outcome.summary: Bitcasino.io remains a live, licensed crypto-first casino after a long operating history. Success means durable service and regulatory continuity, not verified profitability or audited customer balances.

why.summary: The casino combined early crypto payment support with a broad custodial game catalogue, promotions and round-the-clock support. The reviewed evidence supports continuity and product breadth but cannot isolate the contribution of crypto rails.

strategic_choices.decision: Use crypto as a deposit and withdrawal rail inside an operator-controlled casino account.
strategic_choices.consequence: This broadened payment access while retaining centralized KYC, balance, game and withdrawal controls.

strategic_choices.decision: Maintain a broad third-party and in-house casino catalogue under a named regulated operator.
strategic_choices.consequence: Content breadth and regulatory continuity support longevity, while game economics remain opaque.

counterfactual.summary: Without broad game supply and a durable compliance path, a Bitcoin-only novelty casino likely would have had weaker retention and longevity. No controlled cohort evidence quantifies this inference.

watch.signal: CGA certificate and registry status for OGL/2023/111/0069.
watch.implication: A change would alter the verified Curaçao posture without itself proving product failure.
Material changes may affect customer risk and availability.

unknowns: What are audited GGR, net revenue and profitability?
What customer liabilities and reserves does the operator maintain?
How many unique active players use crypto rather than fiat rails?

synthesis.present_situation: Bitcasino.io is active under a named Curaçao operator and current CGA certificate.
synthesis.business_mechanism: A custodial casino takes crypto and fiat deposits and supplies operator-ledger games, promotions and rewards.
synthesis.token_contribution: No official platform token is required for the scoped casino.
synthesis.chain_dependence: Blockchains are payment rails; wagers and balances are operator-controlled.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: The CGA certificate is entity-, domain- and jurisdiction-specific.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Early crypto positioning plus broad content and compliance continuity plausibly support durability.
synthesis.counterfactual: A narrow Bitcoin-only catalogue likely would have limited retention.
lessons_learned: Crypto deposits do not make a casino noncustodial.
Licence claims require entity and domain scope.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers roobet.com operated by Raw Entertainment B.V. It excludes lookalike/localized domains, payment-agent entities, sponsored creators and any inference that the full third-party game catalogue is provably fair on-chain.

sources.notes: Current jurisdiction exclusions; availability is not global.

sources.notes: Official operator, company number, licence number, domain and active-status source.

claims.evidence_locator: Current help page reports 7,848 games, 12 house games, many crypto/fiat rails and 24/7 support.
claims.analyst_note: First-party catalogue count, not players, wagers or revenue.

claims.evidence_locator: CGA certificate identifies Raw Entertainment B.V., company 157205, roobet.com, licence OGL/2024/687/0427 and active status.
claims.analyst_note: Does not license lookalike domains or every jurisdiction.

claims.evidence_locator: Current help article lists numerous prohibited countries and territories.
claims.analyst_note: Prevents describing the product as globally available.

licences.notes: Active certificate for the named entity and domain; territorial restrictions remain.

outcome.label: successful
outcome.summary: Roobet is an active, licensed crypto-first casino and sportsbook with a large current catalogue and multi-asset payment support. This establishes durability, not audited profitability or unrestricted global availability.

why.summary: A differentiated house-game layer, broad third-party catalogue and many crypto rails plausibly support acquisition and retention. Current evidence does not quantify sponsorship, affiliate, bonus or geographic contributions.

strategic_choices.decision: Combine proprietary rapid-cycle games with thousands of third-party casino titles and sportsbook access.
strategic_choices.consequence: The bundle creates differentiation and breadth while keeping customer funds and access under operator control.

strategic_choices.decision: Support many crypto rails while enforcing broad territorial restrictions.
strategic_choices.consequence: Payment reach expands without making service legally available everywhere.

counterfactual.summary: Without proprietary games and catalogue expansion, Roobet likely would have had weaker differentiation from other crypto casinos. No controlled retention analysis was located.

watch.signal: CGA certificate status and named operator.
watch.implication: A change would update the verified legal scope.
Geographic contraction or catalogue decay could weaken the success thesis.

unknowns: What are audited GGR, profitability and customer liabilities?
How many unique active players use Roobet Originals versus third-party games?
How much acquisition depends on promotions, affiliates and sponsorship?

synthesis.present_situation: Roobet remains active under an official CGA certificate with a large current catalogue.
synthesis.business_mechanism: A custodial casino and sportsbook combines proprietary games, third-party content and crypto/fiat payment rails.
synthesis.token_contribution: No official platform token is required.
synthesis.chain_dependence: Chains supply payment rails; the casino account and most games are centralized.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: The Curaçao licence is current for roobet.com, but availability is restricted across many territories.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Originals plus catalogue breadth and payment choice plausibly explain durability.
synthesis.counterfactual: Removing proprietary games likely reduces differentiation.
lessons_learned: Catalogue count is not usage or revenue.
Crypto payment breadth does not erase geographic restrictions.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers the original Etheroll Ethereum dice-game frontend and operating thesis. It does not classify the immutable historical contracts, DICE/ROL token balances, forks, academic datasets or unrelated dice games as inactive.
case.token_utility: Historical Etheroll profit-distribution token; no current distribution or operating utility was established.
case.token_fee_revenue_rights: Historical materials described profit allocation, but no current enforceable revenue stream was verified.

sources.title: etheroll.com parked domain
sources.notes: Current domain says it may be for sale and provides no playable casino.

sources.title: DICE (ROL) ERC-20 contract
sources.notes: Verified historical token code and supply evidence; contract persistence is not product activity.

sources.notes: Historical labelled contract and transaction evidence; not a current frontend.

claims.evidence_locator: Current etheroll.com is a generic parked page stating the domain may be for sale.
claims.analyst_note: Establishes frontend discontinuity, not destruction of contracts or token balances.

claims.evidence_locator: Verified contract identifies EtherollToken, name DICE, symbol ROL and fixed historical supply.
claims.analyst_note: Persistent token code is explicitly excluded from the product-failure conclusion.

claims.evidence_locator: Etherscan labels the historical Etheroll game contract and exposes playerRollDice calls.
claims.analyst_note: Historical transactions prove a shipped product, not current operation.

events.description: Current review found etheroll.com parked with no playable product; exact cessation date remains unknown.

outcome.label: failed
outcome.summary: The original Etheroll dice-game product is inactive: its primary domain is parked and no playable service remains there. Historical contracts and the DICE/ROL token persist and are outside the product-level failure label.

why.summary: Etheroll proved a minimal on-chain casino could ship, but a one-game Ethereum-mainnet experience exposed users to gas, oracle and narrow-product constraints. The reviewed record establishes discontinuity, not a single verified causal shutdown reason.

strategic_choices.decision: Put individual dice wagers and settlement directly on Ethereum.
strategic_choices.consequence: The design created transparent, noncustodial game history but tied user experience to mainnet transaction costs and latency.

strategic_choices.decision: Build a profit-linked token around a single flagship dice product.
strategic_choices.consequence: Token value and utility depended heavily on continuing product economics; token-contract persistence alone could not sustain the casino frontend.

counterfactual.summary: A lower-cost execution layer and broader game catalogue might have improved retention, but no reviewed evidence demonstrates that either would have prevented discontinuity.

watch.signal: A verified relaunch announcement or replacement official domain.
watch.implication: A genuine relaunch could change the inactive classification.

watch.signal: New game-contract transactions tied to an authenticated operator.
watch.implication: Contract activity without operator authentication should not be treated as product recovery.

unknowns: When exactly did the playable frontend cease?
Were final bankroll and token-holder distributions completed?
Who currently controls any administrative keys and official brand assets?
Did gas costs, regulation, competition or team capacity dominate the shutdown?

synthesis.present_situation: The original domain is parked; historical game and token contracts remain visible.
synthesis.business_mechanism: A noncustodial Ethereum dice game settled wagers through smart contracts.
synthesis.token_contribution: DICE/ROL historically linked holders to game economics, but no current distribution was verified.
synthesis.chain_dependence: Direct Ethereum execution provided transparency and imposed mainnet UX costs.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: No current operator or licence was established.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: A narrow product and mainnet-only execution plausibly constrained durability, but causality remains underdetermined.
synthesis.counterfactual: Lower-cost execution and more games might have helped.
lessons_learned: Immutable contracts can outlive a failed product.
Token persistence is not operating recovery.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers Wagerr's consumer sportsbook applications and primary web distribution. It excludes declaring the WGR blockchain, token, source code, community nodes or independently built clients dead merely because the official web and release surfaces are stale or unavailable.
case.token_utility: Native betting, staking, oracle and settlement asset on the Wagerr blockchain.
case.token_fee_revenue_rights: No current unconditional holder revenue right was established.

sources.title: Wagerr Core
sources.notes: Official core design and release history; latest displayed core release is 4.0.0 from December 2020.

sources.title: Wagerr Electron App 2.1.3
sources.notes: Latest official desktop-app release located; absence of later releases is distribution-staleness evidence, not proof the chain halted.

sources.notes: Primary domain did not return a usable product surface during review; transient outage remains possible.

claims.evidence_locator: Repository documents Wagerr Core, its native chain, WGR supply/rewards and public source history.
claims.analyst_note: Source-code persistence contradicts a total-project death claim.

claims.evidence_locator: Latest official electron-app release located is v2.1.3, published February 2022.
claims.analyst_note: Stale releases support decline, not certain protocol cessation.

claims.evidence_locator: Primary domain failed to expose a usable sportsbook during the 2026-07-29 review.
claims.analyst_note: A single review cannot distinguish permanent closure from transient outage.

events.description: Latest located official desktop sportsbook release was v2.1.3; no formal wind-down announcement was established.

outcome.label: declining
outcome.summary: Wagerr's consumer sportsbook distribution is declining: the primary domain was unusable and the latest located official desktop-app release dates to 2022. The open-source chain and token artifacts persist, so this is not a total-project death label.

why.summary: A dedicated betting chain offered transparent settlement but required Wagerr to maintain consensus, oracle, wallet and consumer-distribution layers simultaneously. The record shows stale distribution, but not which operational, liquidity or regulatory constraint dominated.

strategic_choices.decision: Build a purpose-specific blockchain and native WGR economy for sports betting.
strategic_choices.consequence: The design made betting logic transparent but created a full independent network, oracle and wallet maintenance burden.

strategic_choices.decision: Distribute a desktop betting client tied to chain releases.
strategic_choices.consequence: The application exposed native betting features, but a release cadence ending in 2022 left consumer distribution stale.

counterfactual.summary: Building atop a larger chain and using a web-first client might have reduced maintenance and onboarding friction, but no comparative adoption study establishes that this would have solved liquidity or regulatory constraints.

watch.signal: A new signed core or consumer-client release.
watch.implication: Sustained releases could support a recovery classification.

watch.signal: Restoration of wagerr.com with live markets and verifiable chain activity.
watch.implication: A working official sportsbook would contradict frontend inactivity.

unknowns: Is the Wagerr chain currently producing blocks with a healthy validator set?
What current betting volume and active-user count exist?
Was the consumer sportsbook formally discontinued?
Are independent clients still serving bettors?

synthesis.present_situation: Official consumer distribution is stale or unavailable; code and token artifacts survive.
synthesis.business_mechanism: A purpose-built blockchain settles sports bets using WGR and native network roles.
synthesis.token_contribution: WGR is integral to the chain, but token persistence does not establish a healthy sportsbook.
synthesis.chain_dependence: The product depends on a dedicated chain, oracle data, nodes and client distribution.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: No current operator licence or jurisdictional availability was established.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Full-stack network maintenance and consumer-distribution friction plausibly contributed to decline.
synthesis.counterfactual: A larger host chain and web-first distribution might have reduced burden.
lessons_learned: Stale frontends do not prove a blockchain stopped.
A purpose-built chain multiplies maintenance surfaces.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers the Virtue Poker consumer real-money/P2E poker platform launched in 2021. It does not classify Consensys, investors, founders, the VPP token contract, historical player balances or the legal entity and any residual licence as failed.
case.token_utility: Historical poker buy-in, rewards and play-to-earn utility; no current utility was verified.
case.token_fee_revenue_rights: No unconditional current holder revenue right was established.

claims.evidence_locator: Launch review describes Ethereum/sidechain custody design, VPP and limited tables/player liquidity at launch.
claims.analyst_note: Independent contemporaneous review, not current activity evidence.

claims.evidence_locator: Issuer announced a $5 million strategic round to bootstrap the May 2021 mainnet launch.
claims.analyst_note: Financing is not revenue or adoption.

claims.evidence_locator: Primary domain resolved without a usable poker lobby, registration surface or current product content.
claims.analyst_note: Supports product inactivity; exact cessation date remains unknown.

claims.evidence_locator: MGA selector identifies Virtue Gaming Operations Ltd but reviewed output does not state an unambiguous current licence status.
claims.analyst_note: Current licence status is deliberately withheld rather than inferred.

events.description: Virtue Poker launched its Ethereum-based consumer platform.

outcome.label: failed
outcome.summary: Virtue Poker shipped a licensed, Ethereum-linked poker platform but did not establish durable consumer distribution; its primary domain no longer exposes a usable product. The legal entity, historical licence and token are not classified as dead.

why.summary: The strongest evidenced weakness was liquidity at launch: limited tables and unfilled games constrained the network effect required by peer-to-peer poker. Blockchain custody and licensing solved trust and compliance problems but not the cold-start player pool.

strategic_choices.decision: Build nontraditional smart-contract/sidechain custody and peer-to-peer card infrastructure.
strategic_choices.consequence: The design differentiated on transparency but increased onboarding and technical complexity relative to incumbent poker rooms.

strategic_choices.decision: Launch with promotional funding and celebrity/investor credibility before a self-sustaining player pool was visible.
strategic_choices.consequence: Attention and capital supported launch, but contemporaneous review still found thin game liquidity.

counterfactual.summary: A narrower initial geography, scheduled-tournament liquidity and simpler custodial onboarding might have concentrated the player pool enough to cross the cold start. The reviewed evidence does not test this counterfactual.

watch.signal: A verified Virtue Poker relaunch with a live lobby and funded games.
watch.implication: Sustained liquidity could move the case into recovery.

watch.signal: MGA record details for Virtue Gaming Operations Ltd.
watch.implication: A clear status would resolve the current licence unknown without changing historical product inactivity by itself.

unknowns: When exactly did real-money and P2E operations cease?
What is the current VPP supply and utility?
What is the final status of the Virtue Gaming Operations Ltd licence and legal entity?

synthesis.present_situation: The consumer product is inactive at its primary domain; current licence status remains unresolved.
synthesis.business_mechanism: Peer-to-peer poker used Ethereum-linked escrow, sidechain infrastructure and VPP incentives.
synthesis.token_contribution: VPP supported buy-ins/rewards but did not solve player-pool liquidity.
synthesis.chain_dependence: Blockchain custody differentiated the product while increasing onboarding complexity.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: A historical licence claim is documented; current status is withheld pending an unambiguous regulator record.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Cold-start liquidity and complex onboarding plausibly outweighed trust differentiation.
synthesis.counterfactual: Concentrated scheduled liquidity and simpler onboarding might have improved survival.
lessons_learned: Licensing and funding do not solve peer-to-peer liquidity.
An inactive product does not prove its legal entity dissolved.
